evidence: Underground Resistance's anti-major-label, anti-commercial stance is widely described by critics and by Mike Banks himself as a reaction to the increasing commercialization of Detroit techno's first wave, without a specific documented statement naming Atkins individually.

trackPair.whatToListenFor: Atkins' record is cool and controlled; UR's is aggressive and stripped of any pop concession. Same machine vocabulary, opposite emotional register and opposite stance toward the music industry.

explanation: UR rejected the major-label deals that some first-wave Detroit techno artists had started signing, choosing to stay independent and anonymous instead. This is marked as a reaction against, not a direct influence, because UR set themselves against a trend the Belleville Three had begun, crossover success and licensing to major labels, rather than against Atkins personally, so it is held at consensus rather than documented.
